interpretation.headline: Strong-anchor broad-pool rerank fixes the observed lexical-underfetch class as reused-set regression evidence, not as fresh generalization evidence.
interpretation.burned_result_use: The 16-item 2026_08 holdout is burned; its latest rerank run is regression evidence only, not fresh validation.
interpretation.fresh2_result_use: Fresh2 was already burned by earlier committed runs. The f64888b run is reused-set regression evidence after the strong-anchor retrieval fix; a successor holdout is required for any new generalization claim.
interpretation.next_step: Diagnose f006 and f011 answer coverage plus f014 routing/agent escalation on a separate debug set, then verify on a successor fresh holdout. f011 had retrieval_hit=true but relevance_ok=false, so the strong-anchor relevance gate also has one positive-query false negative to calibrate if it affects product behavior.

limitations: Fresh2 has multiple committed runs and is no longer fresh; these metrics are regression evidence on a reused holdout.
Fresh2 was created after inspecting the burned set failure classes; it tests coverage of related failure classes but is not independent of the chosen failure taxonomy.

The relevance denominator contains only answerable positive queries because run_eval does not perform diagnostic retrieval for unanswerable rows; this run measures retrieval sensitivity, not negative-query specificity.
Direct-control rows f001/f002 used min_hits=1, so their contains_pass result should be read with the recorded answer text, not as a standalone behavioral-proof metric.
Route-only and full-pipeline runs use live Gemini output, so exact answer wording may vary across reruns.
